The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Escalation is terminal: no monetary outcome issues, so there is nothing for POL-GEN-05 to execute and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded.

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The deviation is established on the governing trace figure. The GPS polyline measures 27.28 km over a booked optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 5.28 km and 24.00%, so both POL-RD-01 gates pass — more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measure and says the trip record's 27.3 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test, so the excess is 5.28 km, not 5.3 km.

evidence EV-GPS-02809, EV-TRIP-02809 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The trace carrying that measurement is unimpaired, so the rider's showing stands on the trace itself and no escalation for a broken trace arises. It holds 214 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100% coverage, zero gaps, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s and no jump of any size, so none of POL-RD-07's three impairment limbs is met and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

evidence EV-GPS-02809, EV-TRIP-02809 · clauses POL-RD-07, POL-RD-08

The three artifacts describe one trip, so the initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and the burden shifts to the driver.

evidence EV-TRIP-02809, EV-GPS-02809, EV-FARE-02809 · clauses POL-RD-08

The record's own computation of this test states on its face that it decides nothing by itself, and the closure scenario in the fare block is an arithmetic assumption, not a finding that limb (c) is met.

To both parties. Trip TRP-02809 measured 27.28 km on the GPS trace against a booked optimal of 22.0 km — an excess of 5.28 km, or 24%. The trace figure governs (POL-RD-01, EV-GPS-02809); the trip record's 27.3 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and is not used. Both gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%) pass, so a deviation is established, and the trace is unimpaired — 214 fixes, 10-second spacing, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s — so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not escalate it. The driver's closure explanation succeeds under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory ADV-20260907-070 (EV-ADVIS-02809-01) closes the CTE towards the AYE after Braddell Road, on a corridor the optimal route traverses (intersects_route true) — limb (a); its window 20:44:02–22:14:32 overlaps the trip 21:14:02–21:49:32 by 65.5 minutes, far beyond the 15-minute buffers — limb (b); and the actual route did not traverse the affected segment — the trace records 0 fixes inside the advisory area and a closest approach of 1,344.79 m — so it left the optimal corridor before the segment and rejoined it after — limb (c). The optimal route's own polyline is not in the bundle, so the advisory-area computation is the closest test of limb (c) that the record allows; I have weighed it against the limb and it supports it, rather than the closure being assumed from the fare block. The rider's objection that the vehicle was 'nowhere near' the closure is not a defect in the driver's case: a route that avoids a closed segment is expected to stay outside it, and the recorded facts — optimal route traverses the closure, actual trace does not — are what limb (c) asks for. The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the whole excess: cap = 1.30 x (25.6 - 22.0) + 1.00 = 5.68 km; justified excess = min(5.28, 5.68) = 5.28 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is 22.0 + 5.28 = 27.28 km, duration 37.2 min, leaving no excess to refund. Running POL-RD-02 on the adjusted route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 27.28 + 0.28 x 37.2) x 1.0 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, EV-FARE-02809) + 0.80 platform fee = 35.476, which exceeds the 35.02 charged, so the refund floors at zero and is below the 0.50 de minimis. The charged state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) therefore stands. Had the closure not excused the excess, POL-RD-02 on the booked optimal would have recomputed the fare at 29.50 and produced 5.52, rounded up to 5.55 — the rider's figure — but that computation does not apply. The rider's remaining points are answered. The POL-RD-08 burden is discharged: the driver points to a specific artifact (EV-ADVIS-02809-01) and a specific clause (POL-RD-03), which is what that clause requires; the counterparty statement itself adds nothing, and no clause makes it the test of any limb here. The rider's fallback escalation does not fire: POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged because the advisory is in the bundle and covers the trip window, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged because the trace is unimpaired. No POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral: the deviation is not MATERIAL (24% is under 50%, 5.28 km is under 8.0 km), and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 202 (0.005) is far below the 0.05 pattern threshold, with fewer than 3 flags. No POL-RD-09 correction: the fare carries no ERP, toll or surcharge lines (0.00), and there is no billing-integrity defect. POL-RD-11 does not apply (METERED fare, quoted_fare null), and POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 do not apply (the chat log is empty; no pickup or dropoff amendment; amended_optimal_distance_km is null). No driver compensation is due: the billed 27.3 km is not less than the trace's 27.28 km. No clause produces a referral. The monetary effect is nil, so nothing is executed or held and the charge stands.
Both of you: the trip measured 27.28 km on the GPS trace against a booked optimal of 22.0 km — an excess of 5.28 km, or 24% — so the POL-RD-01 gate is passed, and the trace that measures it is clean: 214 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and no jumps, so none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs is met and there is no POL-RD-10(3) escalation. The question is whether the closure on file excuses the extra distance, and it does. EV-ADVIS-02809-01 is a genuine LTA DataMall record: a HIGH-severity two-lane closure on the Central Expressway towards the AYE after Braddell Road, valid 20:44:02 to 22:14:32, overlapping the trip window of 21:14:02 to 21:49:32 by 65.5 minutes — far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03(b) allows. The record states the advisory intersects the route, so the closed segment lies on the corridor the booked optimal route traverses, which is POL-RD-03(a). For POL-RD-03(c), the optimal route's own polyline is not in the bundle; the closest test the record does allow — whether the trace enters the advisory's area — shows the vehicle did not drive the closed segment (0 fixes inside, nearest fix 1,344.79 m away). Read together with the fact that the optimal route does traverse that segment, that is the very signature POL-RD-03(c) asks for: the driver left the corridor before the affected stretch and rejoined it after. The rider's contrary reading — that the vehicle was nowhere near the closure, so the 5.28 km cannot be closure-caused — is not accepted: a route that avoids a closed segment will not enter it, and the nearest-approach figure is the closest test this record allows, not proof that the detour was unrelated. Because the driver points to a specific artifact and a specific clause, POL-RD-08 is discharged and POL-RD-13's uncited-excuse rule does not arise — the advisory is on file. The exoneration is capped, but the cap does not bite. The shortest lawful alternative is 25.6 km against the booked optimal of 22.0 km, so the cap is 1.30 x 3.6 + 1.00 = 5.68 km; the measured excess is 5.28 km, so the justified excess is min(5.28, 5.68) = 5.28 km — the whole of it. Run POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route: base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 27.28 + 0.28 x 37.2 (the booked 30.0 minutes scaled by 27.28/22.0), + 0.80 platform fee = 35.476, against a charged total of 35.02. There is no ERP or toll and no surcharge or waiting fee on this trip, so nothing is added. The refund is charged_total less the recomputed fare, floored at zero: 0.00, below the 0.50 de minimis. POL-RD-09 adds nothing — erp_gantries is empty — and there is no billing-integrity defect, so no referral arises. I do not escalate. POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged: the advisory the driver relies on is in the pool, covers the trip window and carries the fields POL-RD-03 needs; the absent optimal-route polyline is not a field of any cited artifact the clause requires. Ruling on trip TRP-02809, 2026-09-07, Jurong Point to Blk 456 Hougang Ave 10. DEVIATION — ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 requires the test to be run on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, and that figure is 27.28 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km (EV-TRIP-02809): an excess of 5.28 km, or 24.0%. Both establishment gates pass (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal). The trip record's 27.3 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and was not used for the threshold test. CLOSURE DEFENCE (POL-RD-03) — DOES NOT EXONERATE. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260907-070 (EV-ADVIS-02809-01) is a genuine HIGH-severity closure notice, it names the Central Expressway towards the AYE after Braddell Road, and its 20:44:02–22:14:32 window comfortably overlaps the trip, so limbs (a) and (b) are met. Limb (c) is not. It requires the actual route to leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin it after, and this record cannot show that. The optimal route's own polyline is not in the bundle, and the record itself states that the closest available test — whether the trace enters the advisory's area — decides nothing by itself. The trace never comes within 1,344.79 m of the closed segment and records zero fixes inside it; that is consistent with a detour around the closure, but it is equally consistent with a route that never used that corridor, and it does not show where the booked corridor was left or rejoined. The driver's route is also 1.68 km longer than the shortest lawful alternative the advisory names (25.6 km), and the advisory describes a two-lane closure with a diversion rather than a closed road. The burden of an exculpatory clause is the driver's (POL-RD-08), and it is not discharged; the driver's assertion therefore neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because an advisory IS on file, POL-RD-13 does not apply and there is no missing-advisory escalation. The rider's alternative request that this be escalated under POL-RD-10(5) is refused: no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a missing artifact or one that fails to cover the trip window, and no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires — the trace is unimpaired (214 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged either. REFUND — POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and no quoted fare exists, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. Charged total: 35.02. Recomputed fare: (3.80 + 0.75 × 22.0 + 0.28 × 30.0) × 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 3.80 + 16.50 + 8.40 + 0.80 = 29.50. Refund: 35.02 − 29.50 = 5.52, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 5.55. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only 15.76% of the charge, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full one. The rider's filed figure of SGD 4.50 understates the arithmetic the clause fixes. NOTHING ADDED OR NETTED. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), so no pass-through correction arises under POL-RD-09 and the POL-RD-02 figure is the whole remedy. The chat log is empty and no pickup or dropoff was amended, so POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 give nothing, and no driver compensation is due (the distance billed, 27.3 km, is not less than the trace records). REPEAT-DEVIATION CHECK. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 202 completed trips in 90 days — neither the 3-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio — so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established; the deviation is also not MATERIAL (24.0% is under 50%, 5.28 km is under 8.0 km). There is therefore no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The monetary effect, SGD 5.55, is under the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically, subject to the appeal route. This ruling is provisional and made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days.
To both parties — this decides DSP-02809 (trip TRP-02809). THE RIDER HAS PROVED THE DEVIATION. On the governing trace (POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the trip record's rounded 27.3 km, the threshold measure), the trip ran 27.28 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km — an excess of 5.28 km, 24.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation is established. The three instruments describe one trip (TRP-02809, matching pickup and completion timestamps), so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 214 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, zero gaps, no jumps — so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the rider's escalation-safety fallback on that ground does not arise. THE DRIVER'S CLOSURE DEFENCE DOES NOT EXCUSE THE EXCESS. LTA advisory ADV-20260907-070 is on file and complete, and the first two limbs of POL-RD-03 are met: it names the Central Expressway (CTE), its own record shows the closed segment lies on the optimal route, and its window (20:44:02–22:14:32) overlaps the trip (21:14:02–21:49:32) by 65.5 minutes. Limb (c), however, requires an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor BEFORE the affected segment and rejoins it AFTER, and that cannot be established on this record. The optimal route's own path is not in the bundle, and the only related computation — the trace's distance from the advisory area (0 fixes inside, closest approach 1,344.79 m) — is recorded on its face as deciding nothing by itself; the fare block's closure entries are an arithmetic scenario, not a finding that limb (c) holds. Under POL-RD-08 the driver carries the burden of the exculpatory clause and has not discharged it: his filed statement names no evidence ID, and the artifact he cites does not carry the corridor the limb reads. Because the whole of his cap arithmetic — justified excess min(5.28, 1.30 × (25.6 − 22.0) + 1.00) = 5.28 km, closure-adjusted optimal 27.28 km, nil residual excess, recomputed fare 35.48 — depends on limb (c) being met, none of it applies. The rider's fallback to escalation under POL-RD-10(5) is also rejected: the cited advisory is present, covers the trip window and carries every field POL-RD-03 names, so no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or defective artifact, and the absent optimal path is not an artifact the clause is invoked against. THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02, booked optimal route). The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. Charged total: 35.02. Recomputed fare: (3.80 + 0.75 × 22.0 + 0.28 × 30.0) × 1.0, the surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus 0.80 platform fee = 29.50. Refund 35.02 − 29.50 = 5.52, rounded up to SGD 5.55. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and 15.8% of the charge, so PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full refund; the rider's own filed figure of 4.50 understates the arithmetic. Nothing is added or netted off: the fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line, so POL-RD-09 yields no standalone pass-through correction. Neither POL-RD-04 nor POL-RD-05 helps the driver — the chat log is empty and neither endpoint was amended. NO REFERRAL, NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: the deviation is not material (24.0% is below 50%, 5.28 km below 8.0 km) and there is no 90-day pattern (deviation_flags_90d 1 against 202 completed trips, ratio 0.005), so no conduct review and no uplift. POL-RD-09(4) raises no billing-integrity referral (no unmatched line). POL-RD-04 compensation is unavailable: the billed 27.3 km is not less than the trace's 27.28 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall. The monetary effect (SGD 5.55) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, and no safety or complaint flag applies.
